messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: knitr 1.7
parts:
Hi all,

A new version of knitr has been released to CRAN. The changes since
the last version can be found here:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/releases/tag/v1.7 Note only the source
package is available at this moment, and the Windows/OS X binaries are
to come in the next few days, but you can install from the source
package regardless of your OS since knitr is a pure R package:

options(repos = 'http://cran.rstudio.com')
update.packages(ask = FALSE)
if (packageVersion('knitr') < '1.7') install.packages('knitr', type
= 'source')

Please let me know if you have any questions or comments. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: knitr 1.7
parts:
Yes, this is a major change explained in the release notes:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/releases/tag/v1.7

Dan: Sorry, I forgot to update NEWS this time since I always update
NEWS.md (https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/NEWS.md).

In general, package authors are not expected to use hard-coded figure
filenames in their vignettes. I'm aware that some authors have code
like this in their vignettes:

<<foo, include=FALSE>>=
plot(1:10)
@
\begin{figure}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics{figure/foo}
\caption{A figure foo.}
\end{center}
\end{figure}

Since knitr 1.7, the filename will be foo-1 instead of foo. I need to
see some convincing use cases on why the LaTeX code with hard-coded
figure filenames is necessary, because it is entirely possible and
even more compact to write

<<foo, fig.cap="A figure foo.", fig.align="center">>=
plot(1:10)
@

which automatically generates the appropriate LaTeX code with a single
R code chunk, and authors will never need to consider the filenames.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.author: 622493ea5d13c393
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: knitr 1.7
parts:
Dear Yihui

since you asked for use cases. I use the hardcoded figure names a lot, especially when I want to construct a LaTeX float figure that collects multiple plots (subpanels) that were produced in different chunks.
  • Code readability would suffer (a lot) if we necessarily had to produce these in one single chunk, using par(mfrow) or layout and the like
  • The ability to produce nice-looking documents would suffer if we could not use LaTeX (e.g. tables, minipages) to assemble subpanels into multipanel figures.
As far as I understand, it's not too much trouble to add '-1' to the chunk name in legacy documents or new documents. I would appreciate if the name of the produced figure file remains predictable in future versions of knitr (e.g. from the chunk name).

Kind regards
Wolfgang Huber (EMBL)

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: knitr 1.7
parts:
This is rather hidden as a minor change, but it broke quite a few of my reports on recompiling.

..for R Markdown v2 documents, if the inline R output is formatted using the scientific notation, the output must be put in a math environment, e.g. $`r 2e10`$...

I normally do not put constants into inline chunks, but rather variables, and these can switch into scientific mode when changed.

Essentially, this "minor change" means that I must put all inline code into $ for fear it could fall below or above the magical threshold. See also http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26437835.

Also: https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/864

Dieter
